# What Is Synthetic Data?

Source: https://lowob.com/research/what-is-synthetic-data/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-11-01 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Strategy

> Summary: Synthetic data is artificial data generated by algorithms to reproduce the statistical patterns of real data. It is useful for testing, for training where data is scarce, and for sharing without exposing records. The ICO warns it can still be personal data, and research in Nature shows models trained recursively on generated data degrade.

Synthetic data is artificial data produced by an algorithm so that it reproduces the statistical patterns of a real dataset without copying its records. It is used to test systems, to train models where real data is scarce or sensitive, and to share data more safely. It is not automatically anonymous, and it is only as good as the real data and the method behind it.

*Figure: Where this piece sits in The Build Order: the context layer.*

## What synthetic data means

A generator learns the patterns of a real dataset: distributions, correlations, typical combinations of values. It then produces new records that follow those patterns. Analysis run on good synthetic data should give results close to analysis on the original. Partially synthetic data replaces only sensitive fields; fully synthetic data replaces every field.

Large language models have added a second kind. Teams now use a model to write example emails, call transcripts or customer questions, either to test a system or to train another model. These are synthetic too, but they mirror what the generating model has learned, not a particular dataset.

| Synthetic data is | Synthetic data is not |
| --- | --- |
| Generated records that follow real patterns | Real records with names removed |
| Useful where real data is scarce or restricted | Anonymous by default |
| As accurate as the source and the method allow | A source of facts about real customers |

## Where it helps

The ICO notes that synthetic data "can be a useful tool for training AI models in environments where you are not able to access large datasets", and treats it as one of several privacy-enhancing technologies. For a commercial team, three uses are practical.

| Use | Example (illustrative) | Main caution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Testing an agent before it touches live systems | A sandbox CRM filled with synthetic accounts and deals, to test a pipeline clerk's updates | Edge cases in real data may be missing |
| Training and demos | Synthetic call transcripts for onboarding or for a vendor demo | Generated text can sound plausible and be wrong |
| Sharing data with a partner or vendor | A synthetic version of a customer list for a scoping exercise | May still be personal data if records can be inferred |

Regulation now points to it as well. Article 4a of the EU AI Act, added by the Digital Omnibus, allows special categories of personal data to be processed for bias detection and correction only where that "cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data, including synthetic or anonymised data".

## Where it fails

### It can still identify people

Generating synthetic data from a customer database "may involve processing personal information", as the ICO puts it, and the output may still be personal data. The ICO says the answer "depends on whether the personal information on which you model the synthetic data can be inferred from the synthetic data itself". Outliers are the weak point: a customer with an unusual profile can be reproduced closely enough to be recognised. The ICO suggests suppressing outliers or combining synthesis with differential privacy, and notes a trade-off: the more useful the data, the more likely it is to reveal someone. For some tasks, such as fraud detection that depends on outliers, no acceptable balance may exist.

### It can degrade models

Shumailov and colleagues, writing in Nature in July 2024, trained successive generations of models on data produced by the previous generation. The tails of the original distribution, the rare cases, vanished first, and the damage was lasting. They observed the effect in large language models and in simpler model types. The authors suggest that genuine human-generated data will become more valuable as generated text spreads.

For a business, the lesson is narrower than the headline. Synthetic data used to test or supplement is useful. Synthetic data that slowly replaces the real record, without anyone checking it against outcomes, loses exactly the unusual cases that matter most in selling: the odd deal, the unexpected objection, the client that behaves unlike the segment.

## How to use it safely

| Step | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Label synthetic data at source | So it never mixes with real records in the CRM or warehouse |
| Treat generation from personal data as processing | It needs a lawful basis and may need a DPIA |
| Check for re-identification on outliers | They are the most exposed records |
| Validate results on real data before acting | Synthetic patterns can differ from reality |
| Keep it out of training loops by default | Recursive use degrades quality |

## The **lowob** view

Synthetic data belongs in the wiring, not the record. It is a good way to test connectors, permissions and agents before they touch live accounts, which suits the narrow first agent **lowob** recommends; see [The First AI Agent Should Be Boring](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-ai-agent-should-be-boring/). It should never stand in for decisions and outcomes. The learning step of the brain loop depends on what actually happened, and that cannot be generated.

## lowob takeaways

- **Not automatically anonymous.** The ICO says it may be personal data if the source can be inferred.
- **Good for testing.** A synthetic sandbox lets an agent be trialled without live client data.
- **Bad as a replacement for reality.** Recursive training on generated data loses the rare cases first.
- **Label it.** Synthetic records must never mix with the real commercial record.

## Common questions

### What is synthetic data in simple terms?

Artificial data generated by an algorithm to follow the same statistical patterns as real data, without copying the real records.

### Is synthetic data personal data under GDPR?

It can be. The ICO says it depends on whether the original personal information can be inferred from the synthetic data.

### What is model collapse?

The degradation seen when models are trained repeatedly on data generated by earlier models; rare features of the original data disappear first.

### What is synthetic data used for in business?

Testing systems and agents, training models where real data is scarce or restricted, demonstrations, and sharing data with partners more safely.

## Sources and notes

- [ICO, Synthetic data](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/data-sharing/privacy-enhancing-technologies/what-pets-are-there/synthetic-data), 10 September 2025. UK regulator guidance; under review after the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.
- [Shumailov et al., AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data, Nature 631, 755 to 759](https://ideas.repec.org/a/nat/nature/v631y2024i8022d10.1038_s41586-024-07566-y.html), July 2024. Peer-reviewed research; bibliographic record, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07566-y.
- [European Commission AI Act Service Desk, Article 4a](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-4a), consolidated text as at 27 July 2026. Primary legal text; new article added by the Digital Omnibus.

## Related research

- [The First AI Agent Should Be Boring](https://lowob.com/research/the-first-ai-agent-should-be-boring/)
- [What Is an AI Impact Assessment?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-impact-assessment/)
- [What Is CRM Data Hygiene?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-crm-data-hygiene/)
- [What Are AI Evals?](https://lowob.com/research/what-are-ai-evals/)

## Next move

Before your next agent pilot, build a sandbox with 50 synthetic accounts that include a few deliberately odd cases. Run the agent there first, and label every synthetic record so it cannot leak into the live CRM.

# What Is Conversation Intelligence?

Source: https://lowob.com/research/what-is-conversation-intelligence/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-31 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Revenue

> Summary: Conversation intelligence tools record and transcribe sales calls and meetings, then flag topics such as competitor and pricing mentions, next steps and coaching moments. Salesforce and Gong document typical features and consent settings. Recording law and the EU ban on workplace emotion recognition set limits. The value comes when confirmed commitments move into the CRM and the decision record.

Conversation intelligence is software that records, transcribes and analyses sales calls and meetings. It flags topics such as competitor mentions, pricing questions and next steps, and gives managers material for coaching and deal reviews. Its limits are legal as much as technical: recording needs the right consent, and in the EU, inferring employees' emotions at work is prohibited.

*Figure: Where this piece sits in The Build Order: the context layer.*

## What conversation intelligence means

A sales team holds hundreds of conversations a month. Most of what is said never reaches the CRM. Conversation intelligence captures those calls and turns them into searchable text and structured signals.

The typical feature set has four parts. **Capture:** recording calls from a dialler or video meetings. **Transcription:** speech converted to text. **Detection:** flagging keywords, topics, questions and next steps. **Analysis:** dashboards that show trends across calls, such as how often a competitor comes up.

Salesforce's Trailhead module shows the shape. Recordings "undergo processing through our AI system for transcription and detection of insights". Admins choose keywords, and dashboards show "how keywords are trending over time". Competitors are a keyword category, so a manager can see "which competitors are mentioned the most". Recording sources include Salesforce's own dialler and Service Cloud Voice, with other recording systems connecting through partners.

| Conversation intelligence is | It is not |
| --- | --- |
| A record of what was said on calls | A record of what was decided, until someone confirms it |
| A source for coaching and deal reviews | A substitute for a manager listening to key calls |
| A feed of signals into the CRM | The system of record for deals |
| Subject to recording consent law | Exempt because the call is business-to-business |

## Why it matters for a commercial team

The case is that the best evidence about a deal is in the conversation. Objections, pricing questions, named competitors and promised next steps are all spoken before they are typed. A tool that captures them reduces the distance between what the buyer said and what the forecast assumes.

The constraints are legal first.

**Recording consent.** Rules vary by jurisdiction. California's Penal Code section 632 makes it an offence to record a confidential communication "without the consent of all parties", with a fine of up to $2,500 per violation. A team calling buyers across states and countries needs a consent approach that meets the strictest rule it faces. Gong's consent settings show how vendors handle this. A consent page "displays a consent page before the participant joins the meeting". An audio prompt plays when someone joins. Settings are fixed by an admin, and "you can't disable the settings for an individual call".

**Emotion recognition.** Some tools score sentiment or emotion. Article 5(1)(f) of the EU AI Act prohibits AI systems used "to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions", except for medical or safety reasons. Lewis Silkin's summary of the Commission's guidance gives tracking call centre employees' emotions as an example of prohibited use. A firm with EU staff should check what any sentiment feature measures, and about whom.

**Accuracy.** Automatic insights are approximations. Salesforce itself notes that detected next steps "can vary widely by language". A next step a tool infers is a draft, not a commitment.

In **lowob**'s terms, transcripts belong to the store. The useful step is extraction: the commitments, objections and decisions in a call, confirmed by the seller and written to the CRM and the decision record with an owner.

## How to evaluate a conversation intelligence tool

| Criterion | Question to ask |
| --- | --- |
| Capture coverage | Does it record the dialler, video platforms and in-person meetings you use? |
| Consent controls | Can it show consent pages, play prompts and handle refusals per region? |
| Detection | Can admins define keywords, competitors and topics, and check accuracy? |
| Language support | How well does it handle the languages your buyers speak? |
| CRM write-back | Do confirmed next steps and fields land in the CRM, with a person confirming? |
| Emotion features | Can sentiment or emotion scoring be switched off where the law requires? |
| Retention and access | How long are recordings kept, and who can hear them? |

Start with one use: deal reviews on late-stage opportunities, or onboarding new sellers. Measure whether the extracted next steps match what sellers confirm.

## lowob takeaways

- **It captures what was said.** What was decided still needs a person to confirm it.
- **Consent comes first.** Meet the strictest recording rule among the places you call.
- **Check emotion features in the EU.** Inferring employees' emotions at work is prohibited.
- **Value arrives at write-back.** Confirmed commitments belong in the CRM and decision record.

## Common questions

### What is conversation intelligence software?

Software that records, transcribes and analyses sales calls and meetings, flagging topics, keywords, competitors and next steps for sellers and managers.

### What is the difference between conversation intelligence and an AI notetaker?

A notetaker mainly produces summaries of individual meetings. Conversation intelligence adds analysis across many calls, such as keyword trends and coaching.

### Is it legal to record sales calls?

It depends on location. Some jurisdictions, such as California for confidential communications, require the consent of all parties. Check every place you call.

### Can conversation intelligence detect emotions?

Some tools offer sentiment scoring. In the EU, AI systems that infer employees' emotions in the workplace are prohibited except for medical or safety reasons.

## Sources and notes

- [Salesforce Trailhead, Find Out How Einstein Conversation Insights Works](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/einstein-call-coaching/optimize-sales-performance-with-einstein-call-coaching), undated. Vendor training documentation.
- [Gong Help Center, Call recording and consent settings](https://help.gong.io/docs/call-recording-and-consent-settings), undated. Vendor product documentation; not legal advice.
- [California Penal Code section 632, via Justia](https://law.justia.com/codes/california/code-pen/part-1/title-15/chapter-1-5/section-632), 2024 code. Statute text; applies to confidential communications.
- [European Commission AI Act Service Desk, Article 5: Prohibited AI practices](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-5). Official text.
- [Lewis Silkin, Understanding the EU AI Act's prohibited practices](https://www.lewissilkin.com/insights/2025/02/17/understanding-the-eu-ai-acts-prohibited-practices-key-workplace-and-advertising-102k011), 17 February 2025. Law firm summary of the Commission's guidelines.

## Next move

List every place your sellers call buyers from and into. For each, write down the recording consent rule, and check that your current call tool's consent setting meets the strictest one.

# What Is an AI SDR?

Source: https://lowob.com/research/what-is-an-ai-sdr/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-30 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Revenue

> Summary: An AI SDR is software that performs sales development tasks with some autonomy: researching accounts, drafting and sending prospecting emails, answering replies and booking meetings. Salesforce and HubSpot both ship versions. The evaluation questions are less about writing quality than about sending controls, deliverability, consent law and whether the vendor's own claims can be checked.

An AI SDR is an AI agent that does the work of a sales development representative: it researches target accounts, writes and sends prospecting emails, answers replies and books meetings for human sellers. Products differ mainly in how much they may do without a person. The safe starting point is to let it research and draft, and to have a person approve every message before it sends.

*Figure: Agents are the reasoning layer, and they touch every stage of the build.*

## What an AI SDR means

A sales development representative does the early part of outbound sales. The role finds accounts that fit, identifies the right people, writes first messages, follows up and hands qualified conversations to an account executive. An AI SDR is software that does some or all of those steps.

The category sits between two older tools: a sales engagement platform sends sequences a person writes, and a data provider supplies contacts and signals. An AI SDR adds the writing and the decision about what to send next.

Two large CRM vendors show the range. Salesforce's Agentforce SDR agent has three topics: Send Outreach, Respond to Prospect and Manage Opt-Out. It runs under a dedicated SDR agent user, and event logs record its conversations. HubSpot's prospecting agent detects "companies that match the buying signals that are most important to you", identifies contacts and generates "personalized outreach based on CRM data". Admins set a daily limit on new contacts and a maximum number of emails. Each lead's outreach consumes HubSpot Credits, a usage charge on top of the seat.

| Task | What the AI SDR does | Suggested autonomy level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account and contact research | Finds fitting accounts and people from signals and CRM data | 0 or 1 |
| First-touch email | Drafts personalised outreach | 1 (draft) or 2 (send on approval) |
| Follow-ups in a sequence | Writes and schedules later steps | 2 |
| Replies to prospects | Answers questions, handles opt-outs | 2; opt-outs can run at 3 |
| Meeting booking | Offers times and books calendars | 2 or 3 once error rates are known |

## Why it matters for a commercial team

Outbound volume is cheap to raise and expensive to repair. Three constraints decide the outcome.

**Deliverability.** Mailbox providers judge the sending domain, not the software. Google's sender guidelines require bulk senders, those sending more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts, to use SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Spam rates in Postmaster Tools should stay below 0.10% and never reach 0.30%. Marketing messages must support one-click unsubscribe. An agent that sends at scale from the company's main domain puts all of the firm's email at risk.

**Consent law.** Rules differ by country and by recipient. In the UK, the ICO says the PECR rule on electronic mail marketing "does not apply to corporate subscribers". Sole traders and some partnerships are treated as individuals and need consent or the soft opt-in. Every message must identify the sender and give a valid opt-out address. The UK GDPR applies wherever the email address identifies a person.

**Vendor claims.** The category is young, and claims are hard to verify. In March 2025, TechCrunch reported that 11x had shown logos of companies, including ZoomInfo and Airtable, that said they were not customers or had only trialled the product. 11x said it had "promptly removed any undesired or inaccurate customer mentions" when asked. The lesson for buyers is general: ask for references you can call.

## How to evaluate an AI SDR

| Criterion | Question to ask |
| --- | --- |
| Sending controls | Can every message require approval, and can that be set per task? |
| Limits | Are there daily caps on new contacts and emails, set by the buyer? |
| Domain and authentication | Which domain sends, and are SPF, DKIM and DMARC in place? |
| Opt-outs | Are unsubscribes honoured across all tools and written back to the CRM? |
| Sources | Does each message show the signals and data it relied on? |
| Write-back | Are activities and outcomes recorded in the CRM as the system of record? |
| Pricing | Is it per seat, per lead, per credit or per meeting? |
| References | Can you speak to two current customers at a similar size? |

Start narrow. Pick one segment, let the agent research and draft, and have a named person approve each message for the first few weeks. Track edit rates, replies and unsubscribes per batch. Raise autonomy only on tasks where the record supports it.

## lowob takeaways

- **An AI SDR writes and decides, not just sends.** That is what separates it from a sequencing tool.
- **Deliverability is the first risk.** Authentication, spam rates and unsubscribes apply to every message it sends.
- **Consent rules vary by recipient.** Corporate subscribers, sole traders and named individuals are treated differently in the UK.
- **Verify the vendor.** Call references before relying on logos.

## Common questions

### What does an AI SDR do?

It researches prospects, writes and sends outreach emails, replies to prospects and books meetings, with varying degrees of human approval.

### Can an AI SDR replace human SDRs?

It can take on research, drafting and routine replies. Judgment on targeting, tone and when to hand over still needs a person, and approval of outbound messages is the safer default.

### Is cold email from an AI SDR legal?

It depends on the country and recipient. In the UK, emailing corporate subscribers does not need PECR consent, but emailing sole traders does, and every message needs sender identification and an opt-out.

### How are AI SDRs priced?

Models vary: per seat, per lead, per credit or per meeting booked. HubSpot's prospecting agent, for example, consumes credits for each lead.

## Sources and notes

- [Salesforce Trailhead, Configure and Activate Your Agentforce SDR Agent](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/projects/build-an-agent-to-nurture-leads/configure-and-activate-your-agentforce-sdr-agent), undated. Vendor training documentation.
- [HubSpot Knowledge Base, Use the prospecting agent](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/prospecting/use-the-prospecting-agent?cid=482), undated. Vendor product documentation.
- [Google Workspace Admin Help, Email sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/a/answer/81126?hl=en-GB), undated. Mailbox provider requirements; bulk sender rules effective February 2024.
- [UK Information Commissioner's Office, Business-to-business marketing](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/). Regulator guidance; UK only.
- [TechCrunch, a16z- and Benchmark-backed 11x has been claiming customers it doesn't have](https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/24/a16z-and-benchmark-backed-11x-has-been-claiming-customers-it-doesnt-have), 24 March 2025. News report based on sources and company statements; includes the company's response.

## Related research

- [AI Agents in Sales: What They Can Do Now, Task by Task](https://lowob.com/research/ai-agents-in-sales-what-they-can-do-now/)
- [Gateway 1: Nothing Sends Without a Person](https://lowob.com/research/nothing-sends-without-a-person/)

## Next move

Before any trial, check your sending domain's SPF, DKIM and DMARC records and its current spam rate in Google Postmaster Tools. If any is missing or high, fix that before an agent sends a single message.

# Account Planning for the Top Twenty

Source: https://lowob.com/research/account-planning-for-the-top-twenty/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-29 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Revenue

> Summary: Key account programmes underperform with unusual consistency: Gartner found 58% of B2B sales organisations missing quota on key accounts and most rebuilding their programmes repeatedly. The causes are selection by size of spend, plans that are written once, and coordination that stops at the sales team. This piece sets out a selection rule, a one-page plan, a monthly review and the record that makes each plan a set of decisions rather than a document.

Account planning for the top twenty is the discipline of choosing the twenty or so customers with the most room to grow, writing a short plan for each, and reviewing those plans monthly with the people who serve the account. The evidence says most firms get the selection wrong and the cadence wrong. Gartner found customers chosen as key accounts mainly for their large spend were 51% less likely to increase it, and that organisations which update plans frequently and use them in customer decisions are three times more likely to build the customer's decision confidence. Pick by potential, keep the plan to a page, and review it every month.

*Figure: The wiring turns nine places into one brief. It cannot retrieve a decision nobody wrote down; that is the record's job.*

Most firms of 20 to 500 people know who their largest customers are. Fewer have decided which customers deserve a plan, and fewer still keep those plans current after the first quarter. The result is familiar: a set of documents written during annual planning, read once in a review, and consulted again a year later.

[*What is account planning?*](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-account-planning/) covers the definition and the contents of a plan. This piece covers how to run planning for a defined set of accounts as a routine: how to choose them, how short the plan should be, and how the monthly review turns it into decisions.

## Why key account programmes keep being rebuilt

Gartner's research on key accounts, reported in 2021, is unusually blunt. In a survey of 69 chief sales officers, 95% expected higher growth from key accounts than from other customers. Yet 58% of B2B sales organisations missed quota on those accounts, and 46% had rebuilt their key account programme two or more times in seven years because it underperformed. Gartner's current summary puts the share that have rebuilt at least once in seven years at 79%.

Gartner's diagnosis, as reported by CRM Magazine, is a sales-centric view: key accounts are chosen and managed by the sales team, when what they need is a commitment from the wider firm. The supporting figure is that key account managers reporting high cross-functional collaboration saw roughly three times higher spend from key customers, while 66% of key account managers say internal coordination limits their ability to plan.

Academic research reaches a similar conclusion from a different direction. Homburg, Workman and Jensen's cross-industry, cross-national study in the Journal of Marketing identified eight distinct ways firms organise key account management and found significant performance differences between them, which suggests the design of the routine matters as much as the effort put into it.

That points to three failures, and the rest of this piece addresses them in order: the wrong accounts, a plan nobody uses, and a review that includes only sellers.

## Choosing the twenty

Twenty is a working number, not a rule. It is about as many plans as a revenue leader can review in depth each month, and in most mid-size firms it covers a large share of revenue. A firm of 30 people may have eight; a firm of 300 may have forty split across two leaders.

The selection should weigh growth potential and the firm's ability to capture it, which Gartner calls opportunity alignment. Size of current spend is one input, not the criterion.

| Criterion | What to look at | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Headroom | Estimated total spend in your category minus what you already have | The account must have room to grow |
| Fit | How closely the account matches your ideal customer profile | Growth is cheaper where you already deliver well |
| Relationship breadth | Number of senior contacts and functions you serve | Single-threaded accounts are fragile |
| Strategic intent | Whether the customer is investing in the problem you solve | Budget follows priorities |
| Health | Delivery satisfaction, usage, open issues | You cannot expand an unhappy account |
| Current spend | Revenue in the last twelve months | Protects what matters today, but should not decide alone |

Score each candidate on a simple scale and choose the top twenty, then check the list against revenue concentration. If the list leaves out an account that represents a large share of revenue, protect it with a retention plan rather than a growth plan. [*How to write an ICP*](https://lowob.com/research/how-to-write-an-icp/) covers how to define fit so it can be scored consistently.

Re-tier twice a year. Gartner's own recommendation is to monitor relationship health and move accounts out of the programme when they stop performing, rather than overinvesting in them.

## The one-page plan

A plan that runs to twenty slides will not be read monthly. A plan that fits on one page will.

| Section | Contents | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The customer's goal | What the customer is trying to achieve this year, in their words | Account lead |
| Where we help | The two or three places your work connects to that goal | Account lead |
| Decision map | Who decides, who influences, who is sceptical, and how well you know each | Account lead and delivery lead |
| Objectives | Two to four objectives, each with a measure and a date | Account lead |
| Actions | The next action for each objective, with an owner from any function | Named owners |
| Risks | What could lose the account or stall growth | Account lead and delivery lead |
| Last review | Date, what changed, what was decided | Account lead |

Two features matter more than the rest. The customer's goal comes first, so the plan starts from the customer's agenda rather than your product list. And actions can be owned by anyone, including delivery, finance or a partner, which is how the plan carries the cross-functional coordination that Gartner found so often missing.

The plan also inherits from earlier parts of this series. The decision map and risks start from the handover pack described in Part 27. Renewal dates and expansion targets connect to Part 24. Each objective is, in effect, a commercial decision, and should be recorded as one.

> An account plan is a set of decisions about one customer. If none of them has an owner and a date, it is a description.

## The monthly review

The review is where plans either stay alive or quietly die. Gartner reports that organisations which update account plans frequently, and rely on them to guide customer decisions, are three times more likely to build customer decision confidence, and that customers with high decision confidence are ten times more likely to make a high-quality, low-regret purchase.

CRM vendors say the same about the document itself. Salesforce's training module on account plans calls the plan "a living document" and says "This isn't a one-time exercise", but sets no review schedule, which is the gap a monthly cadence fills. Its suggested contents (an account vision, the customer's priorities and success metrics, and the competitive landscape) map onto the one-page plan above.

A monthly review for twenty accounts can be done in under two hours if it is disciplined.

**Review by exception.** Each account lead reports only what changed: an objective's status, a new risk, a stakeholder change. Accounts with no change take thirty seconds.

**Include delivery.** The delivery lead for each account attends, or sends a written note. That is where health issues surface before they reach the renewal.

**Decide, then record.** Each review should produce decisions: pursue an opportunity, add a senior sponsor, pause expansion until an issue is fixed. Each decision gets an owner and a check date in the record.

**Update the page in the meeting.** The plan's "last review" line is updated before the meeting ends. A plan that is updated afterwards usually is not.

McKinsey's 2024 B2B Pulse survey of nearly 4,000 decision makers found buyers using an average of ten interaction channels, up from five in 2016, and suggested that large, important accounts may benefit from a dedicated representative plus self-service. For the top twenty, the review is where that coverage is set: who owns each relationship, and which channels the customer actually uses.

## Why the effort pays

The economic case for account planning rests on retention and expansion rather than new logos. Fred Reichheld's work at Bain found that in financial services a 5% increase in customer retention produced more than a 25% increase in profit. The figure is old and sector-specific, and it is often stretched beyond what it says. The mechanism holds more widely: retained customers cost less to serve and buy more over time.

For recurring-revenue firms the same logic shows in net revenue retention. SaaS Capital's 2025 benchmarks put median net revenue retention at 102% for private companies with annual contract values of $25,000 to $50,000, and found groups with retention of 110% or more grew faster than the median. Expansion has to come from somewhere, and account planning concentrates effort on the customers with the most headroom rather than spreading it evenly.

| Programme health signal | Healthy | Warning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plans reviewed in the last month | All twenty | Fewer than fifteen |
| Objectives with an owner and a date | All | Some with neither |
| Actions owned outside sales | Several per plan | None |
| Accounts re-tiered in the last six months | Some moved in and out | List unchanged for a year |
| Decisions recorded from reviews | Several a month | None |

## The plan as a record

An account plan is one of the clearest cases of a commercial record that a firm already writes and then fails to keep. The objectives are decisions. The review is where their status is updated. The outcome, expansion or retention, arrives within a year.

That makes it a natural place for the record and the context layer to meet. The figure above shows the problem: an account's history sits across inboxes, call recordings, proposal versions and memory. The context layer can assemble the brief before each review. It cannot supply the reason the firm chose to pursue one opportunity and not another. That is the account lead's job, written in the plan.

Illustrative example: moving an account out of the twenty

Decision
:   Move the second-largest account from the growth programme to a retention plan, and add a smaller account with more headroom.

Reason and owner
:   The account had little category spend left to win and a single senior contact; the replacement scored higher on headroom and strategic intent. Owned by the revenue lead, agreed with the chief executive.

What changed
:   The large account keeps a quarterly retention review with its delivery lead. The new account gets a full plan and a named executive sponsor; both are checked at the next re-tiering.

Illustrative: a composite of a mid-size B2B technology firm, built from patterns across engagements.

## lowob takeaways

- **Select by potential, not spend.** Large current spend predicts less growth than most firms expect.
- **Keep the plan to one page.** The customer's goal first, then objectives with owners and dates.
- **Review monthly, with delivery in the room.** Report by exception and decide before the meeting ends.
- **Record each objective as a decision.** Owner, status and check date turn a plan into evidence.

Gateway card

### Before you call it a key account programme

- A written selection rule weighing headroom, fit and health as well as spend
- One-page plans for every account on the list
- At least one action per plan owned outside sales
- A monthly review with delivery represented
- Decisions from each review recorded with an owner and a check date
- A re-tiering date in the calendar, twice a year

## Common questions

### How many key accounts should a company have?

As many as the revenue leader can review in depth each month, often around twenty for a mid-size firm. Smaller firms may have eight to ten; larger ones may split forty or more across several leaders.

### How do you choose key accounts?

Weigh growth potential and your ability to capture it, not just current spend. Gartner found customers chosen mainly for large spend were 51% less likely to increase it over time.

### How often should account plans be reviewed?

Monthly for the top accounts, by exception, with delivery represented. Gartner reports that organisations which update plans frequently are three times more likely to build customer decision confidence.

### What should a key account plan include?

The customer's goal in their words, where you help, a decision map, two to four objectives with measures and dates, owned actions, risks, and the date and outcome of the last review.

Trade press coverage of Gartner research.

# The Build Order for Healthcare and Life Sciences

Source: https://lowob.com/research/the-build-order-for-healthcare-and-life-sciences/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-29 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Strategy

> Summary: Healthcare and life sciences is one of two sectors where The Build Order bends. HIPAA's marketing rules, state consumer health data laws, FDA promotional enforcement and Open Payments reporting mean the walls, the review gate and the record must exist before any commercial agent. The first agent works for the review committee, not the field team, and patient data never reaches the commercial build.

Healthcare and life sciences is one of the two sectors where The Build Order bends. Here compliance comes first: privacy and promotional review precede any commercial agent. HIPAA requires written authorisation before protected health information is used for most marketing. Washington's My Health My Data Act requires affirmative consent before consumer health data is even collected. FDA's promotion office sent nearly 100 enforcement letters in a single week in September 2025, against five in each of 2023 and 2024. So the walls, the review gate and the record are built before the first agent, and the first agent works for the review committee rather than the field team. Patient data never reaches the commercial build.

*Figure: Gateway 0 is three decisions. Nothing gets bought until all three are answered.*

In most sectors this series starts on the commercial line because decisions there are frequent, quickly graded and defended by a budget holder. In healthcare and life sciences the first decisions a firm must defend are compliance decisions. A regulator, a plaintiff or a journalist may ask why a patient received a message, why a clinician was shown a claim, or why a payment to a physician was not reported. The record has to exist before anything is automated.

This edition runs the sequence for firms of 20 to 500 people: digital health companies, specialty pharmaceutical and medtech firms, clinic groups and health services businesses. It covers the US rules that set the walls, the review gate that comes first, and what remains of the commercial build once those are in place. It is not legal advice; every firm here needs its privacy officer and regulatory counsel at Gateway 0.

## Why the order bends

Part 1 listed eight industries and noted that the order holds in most and bends in two. Financial services moves the record ahead of the first agent because a supervisor may ask the firm to reconstruct any automated decision. Healthcare and life sciences bends further. The walls and the review gate move to Gateway 0, ahead of tooling and context, because a single connection made in the wrong order can be a violation in itself.

The rules that drive this are specific.

**HIPAA's marketing rules.** HHS guidance states that a covered entity generally needs an individual's written authorisation before using or disclosing protected health information for marketing. Communications about treatment, care coordination and the entity's own health-related services are excluded from the definition. But where a third party pays the covered entity to promote its product, the communication is marketing with no exceptions, and the authorisation must state that payment is involved. A covered entity may not sell patient lists without each person's authorisation.

**Consumer health data outside HIPAA.** Many digital health firms are not covered entities. The FTC's amended Health Breach Notification Rule, effective since 29 July 2024, clarifies that it reaches many health apps and connected devices, and that a breach includes an unauthorised disclosure, such as sharing health data with third parties in ways that conflict with the company's own promises. Washington's My Health My Data Act, in effect since 31 March 2024, requires affirmative consent before consumer health data is collected or shared and a separate authorisation before it is sold, and it gives consumers a private right of action.

**Tracking and the website.** HHS guidance on online tracking technologies was partly vacated by a federal court in Texas on 20 June 2024 in *American Hospital Association v. Becerra*, which held that metadata from unauthenticated public web pages is not individually identifiable health information. The court left in place HHS's position that tracking on authenticated pages, such as patient portals, can involve protected health information.

**Security.** The proposed overhaul of the HIPAA Security Rule, the first major update in more than a decade, would require encryption, multifactor authentication and network segmentation among other controls. Fierce Healthcare reported that the OMB website now lists July 2027 for the final rule, a year later than planned. A firm choosing AI vendors now should assume those controls will be expected.

| Industry lens | Healthcare and life sciences |
| --- | --- |
| Where the commercial line sits | Providers and digital health: patient acquisition, referral development, employer and payer contracts. Life sciences: clinician engagement, account management, promotional materials |
| The store | CRM for field teams or referral development; EHR and patient systems held separately |
| What makes it harder | Patient data is regulated wherever it sits, and promotional claims need review before use |
| Outcome lag | Months for referrals, prescriptions and contracts |
| Who defends the decision | Privacy officer, MLR committee, compliance, commercial lead |
| The sector's wall | Patient data from care, portals and patient support programmes; medical information kept apart from sales |
| Regulatory pressure | HIPAA, FTC Health Breach Notification Rule, state consumer health data laws, FDA promotion rules, Open Payments |

## The bent order, stage by stage

| Stage | What it means in healthcare and life sciences | The main risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway 0 | Owner, suite and CRM, plus the privacy officer and MLR lead named as approvers, and the patient data wall drawn | Treating compliance as a review at the end rather than a decision at the start |
| Compliance first | Every source classified as patient data or not; business associate agreements in place with any AI vendor that will touch patient data | An assistant connected to a shared drive that holds patient exports |
| Gateway 1, early | The MLR gate and the approved claims library exist before any agent drafts anything | Agents producing content faster than review can absorb |
| Tooling | Assistant seats for commercial staff, configured without access to patient systems | Seats issued on a suite that already indexes clinical files |
| Context | CRM, approved materials, claims library and references, field call notes | Free-text call notes that contain patient details |
| Record | MLR decisions with claim, reference, approver and expiry; transfers of value; marketing communications with their legal basis | A record of approvals with no link to where the material was used |
| Reasoning | A first agent that checks drafts against approved claims before MLR review | A field-facing agent that paraphrases approved content into unapproved claims |
| Gateway 2 | Value at stake and outcomes on commercial decisions, using leading indicators chosen with care | Optimising for call volume because prescriptions lag |
| Gateway 3 | The record extends to market access and finance; medical affairs stays separate | Commercial reasoning reaching medical information responses |

**Compliance first means classification first.** Before any assistant is connected, each source is classified: does it contain patient data, and under which regime? A vendor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits protected health information for a covered entity is a business associate and needs a business associate agreement. Many general-purpose assistants are not configured for that by default. The simplest design keeps patient data out of the commercial suite entirely, so the question never arises for the commercial build. *The pilot that survives security review* covers the vendor questions to ask.

> In healthcare, the wall and the review gate are not controls added to the build. They are the first thing built.

## The walls

Three walls apply across the sector.

**Patient data and the commercial build.** Clinical records, portal activity and patient lists stay out of the commercial context layer unless a specific authorisation covers the use. In life sciences the same applies to patient support programmes, which often hold names, conditions and insurance details collected to help patients start therapy. Field teams may need to know that a clinic's patients are enrolling. They must never see who.

**Medical information and sales.** Most life sciences firms already separate medical affairs from commercial teams, so that answers to clinicians' scientific questions are not shaped by sales goals. An assistant that reads both a field rep's call notes and the medical information database erases that line, whatever the permissions technically allow. The two context layers should never meet.

**Unreviewed claims and the outside world.** In the promotional setting, a claim is either approved for a use or it is not. An agent that rewords an approved claim has created a new one.

| What the commercial context layer can hold | What it must never hold |
| --- | --- |
| CRM accounts, clinicians' public professional details, call logs without patient details | Clinical records, portal activity or patient lists without authorisation |
| Approved materials, the claims library and references | Draft claims that have not passed MLR review |
| Transfers of value to clinicians, for reporting | Patient support programme data about individuals |
| Aggregate enrolment or referral counts | Medical information requests and responses |

## Promotional review is the commercial line's gate

In life sciences, Gateway 1 already exists. Every promotional piece passes MLR review before use, and the question is whether review can keep up once drafting is cheap.

The enforcement climate makes that question sharper. Hall Render's review of 2025 reports that FDA's Office of Prescription Drug Promotion released nearly 100 enforcement letters, untitled and warning letters together, in a single week in September 2025, against five in each of 2023 and 2024. The firm expects continued scrutiny of digital, influencer and short-form content, and of visual and tonal elements as well as claims, and advises involving promotional review at every stage of creative development.

IQVIA, which sells MLR services, argued in July 2026 that content production is no longer the constraint: review and approval are. It describes agents that check content against approved claims, verify references and flag inconsistencies, and it argues that readiness, not technology, is the barrier, because reference libraries often hold duplicates and outdated documents. We treat that as vendor perspective, but it matches what we see. *Approval rate measures fatigue too* describes what happens when a review queue doubles.

That is why the first agent in this sector works for the review committee. It takes a draft, matches every claim against the approved claims library, checks that each reference is current, and flags anything new before the draft reaches MLR. It writes nothing for a clinician or patient. It shortens review without loosening it.

## The record and the commercial build

Once the walls and the gate exist, the commercial build resumes. The record carries three kinds of decision.

1. **MLR decisions**: the material, each claim, its reference, the approvers, the approval date and the expiry or withdrawal date.
2. **Transfers of value**: meals, fees and other payments to clinicians, which manufacturers already report. CMS's Open Payments data published in 2026 covers $14.67bn across 17.07 million records. A record that links each payment to the engagement that caused it makes reporting a by-product rather than a project.
3. **Marketing communications that use patient data**: for providers and digital health firms, each campaign with its legal basis (authorisation, or an exception such as treatment or care coordination), and the opt-in status of the audience.

Commercial decisions then follow the pattern in Part 9: which accounts to prioritise, which referral relationships to develop, which contracts to pursue. Outcomes lag by months. Part 2 warned that long cycles fail the "quickly graded" test, and the workaround is leading indicators chosen with care. In this sector, call volume is the wrong one, because a system optimises whatever proxy it is given.

Composite example: a specialty pharma firm builds the gate first

Decision
:   Build the approved claims library and an MLR pre-check agent before giving the field team any assistant; keep the patient support programme and medical information on separate systems with no commercial connector.

Reason and owner
:   Review cycle times had doubled as the marketing team began drafting with general-purpose AI. Owned by the head of commercial operations, with the MLR chair and privacy officer as named approvers.

What changed
:   Drafts reach MLR with every claim matched to the library and new claims flagged. Field call notes are now structured fields, so no free text containing patient details reaches the CRM.

Illustrative: a composite of a specialty pharmaceutical firm of around 250 people, built from patterns across engagements.

## lowob takeaways

- **Compliance comes first.** Draw the patient data wall and name the privacy and MLR approvers at Gateway 0.
- **Classify every source before connecting it.** If patient data is present, keep it out of the commercial suite or put a business associate agreement in place.
- **Build the review gate before the agent.** Cheap drafting makes MLR the bottleneck; the first agent should make review faster, not bypass it.
- **Record approvals and payments.** MLR decisions and transfers of value are already required; linking them to engagements makes the record useful.

Gateway card

### Before a healthcare or life sciences firm connects any AI tool

- Privacy officer and MLR lead named as approvers at Gateway 0
- Every source classified for patient data and the regime that applies
- Business associate agreements in place, or patient data excluded from the commercial suite
- An approved claims library with references and expiry dates
- Medical information and patient support programmes on systems with no commercial connector
- A written rule that no agent drafts content for clinicians or patients

## Common questions

### Can healthcare marketers use AI with patient data under HIPAA?

Only within HIPAA's rules. Most uses of protected health information for marketing need the patient's written authorisation, and any marketing paid for by a third party needs authorisation that discloses the payment. Any AI vendor handling the data for a covered entity needs a business associate agreement.

### What is MLR review in pharma?

Medical, legal and regulatory review is the process by which promotional materials are checked for accuracy, balance and compliance before use. With AI making drafting cheaper, review capacity has become the main constraint on promotional content.

### Does HIPAA apply to health apps?

Often not, but other rules do. The FTC's Health Breach Notification Rule covers many health apps outside HIPAA, and treats unauthorised sharing as a breach. Washington's My Health My Data Act requires affirmative consent before consumer health data is collected or shared.

### When will the new HIPAA Security Rule be final?

Fierce Healthcare reported that the OMB website lists July 2027 for the final rule, a year later than planned. The proposal would require encryption, multifactor authentication and network segmentation among other controls.

# What Is a Sales Compensation Plan?

Source: https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-sales-compensation-plan/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-28 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Revenue

> Summary: A sales compensation plan is the written set of rules that turns a seller's results into pay. Its main parts are target pay, the split between base and incentive, the upside for over-performance, the measures, the quota and the payout curve. Survey data from WorldatWork and the Alexander Group shows typical choices, and field research shows that design changes behaviour in predictable ways.

A sales compensation plan is the written set of rules that decides how a seller's results turn into pay. It fixes target earnings, the split between base salary and incentive, the upside available for over-performance, which results count, the quota, and how payout rises or falls with attainment. Sellers read the plan more closely than any strategy document, so the plan is where strategy either reaches the field or does not.

*Figure: Where this piece sits: the commercial line, where the build starts.*

## What a sales compensation plan means

Every plan answers the same questions.

| Component | Question it answers | Common practice in the survey data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Target total compensation | What does a seller earn at 100% of quota? | Set from the labour market for the role |
| Pay mix | How much is base, how much at risk? | 54/46 for field new-account sellers; 66/34 for first-line managers (WorldatWork, 2022) |
| Upside (leverage ratio) | What can a top performer earn? | Often three times the target incentive (Alexander Group) |
| Measures | Which results count? | Two or three measures in 71% of plans |
| Quota | What result earns target pay? | See [Sales Capacity and Quota Setting](https://lowob.com/research/sales-capacity-and-quota-setting/) |
| Payout curve | How does pay change with attainment? | Thresholds in about 60% of plans; regressive rates above a level in 45% |
| Caps and windfall rules | What happens on unusually large deals? | Caps in 50%; mega-deal policies in 46% |
| Crediting rules | Who gets credit when several people touch a deal? | Written split rules, decided before the deal |

The Alexander Group defines mix as the relationship between base salary and the incentive part of target pay, written as two parts of 100%. It defines the leverage ratio as the total incentive available for outstanding performance, expressed as a multiple of the target incentive.

## How it works

A worked example from the Alexander Group shows how the numbers fit.

| Performance | Base | Incentive | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target pay, 70/30 mix | $70,000 | $30,000 | $100,000 |
| Poor performer | $70,000 | $0 | $70,000 |
| At quota | $70,000 | $30,000 | $100,000 |
| Top performer, 90th percentile, 3x | $70,000 | $90,000 | $160,000 |

The firm suggests that in a well-designed uncapped plan, fewer than 10% of sellers should earn above the upper upside amount. If many more do, the quota or the payout curve is the first place to look.

Mix follows the sale. The Alexander Group describes higher-base plans for complex technical sales, long cycles and government buyers. WorldatWork's data shows the same pattern: field sellers chasing new accounts carry more pay at risk than sellers managing current customers, at 46% against 41%.

## Why it matters for a commercial team

### The plan changes behaviour

Thomas Steenburgh and Michael Ahearne's research divides sales forces into laggards, core performers and stars. In field data from a Fortune 500 company, replacing quarterly bonuses with annual ones cut laggards' revenue by about 10%. Ahearne's experiment found tiered targets pushed core performers to sell more. Caps led stars to stop selling once they hit target, and Steenburgh recommends higher commission rates that apply only above target.

### Quota realism decides whether the plan pays

The 2023 Alexander Group survey, reported by WorldatWork, found a gap of 18 points between planned and projected attainment. A plan built on a quota most sellers miss pays out less than designed, and the incentive stops motivating. [Sales Capacity and Quota Setting](https://lowob.com/research/sales-capacity-and-quota-setting/) covers how to build quota from ramp and attainment.

### Profit and price belong in the plan

The same survey found 71% of respondents included profitability in sales manager or seller plans, mostly as a modifier. A plan that pays on bookings alone rewards discounting. Linking pay to realised price is one of the controls set out in [Discount Governance](https://lowob.com/research/discount-governance/).

> Sellers follow the plan, not the strategy deck. If the two disagree, the plan wins.

## How to check your plan

| Test | Warning sign |
| --- | --- |
| Can a seller calculate their own pay from the plan document? | Payouts need a finance query |
| Do measures match the strategy for the year? | Strategy says retention; plan pays only new bookings |
| Is renewal and expansion ownership stated? | Two roles both expect credit; see [Renewals and Expansion](https://lowob.com/research/renewals-and-expansion/) |
| Are crediting splits written before deals close? | Splits are negotiated after signature |
| How many sellers exceeded the upside last year? | Far more or far fewer than about one in ten |

In **lowob**'s model the plan is one of the yearly decisions worth recording, with its reasoning, owner and expected attainment, and graded at year end. Credit disputes and windfall rulings are smaller decisions of the same kind. An agent can draft commission statements and flag disputes at autonomy level 1 or 2. Who gets paid what stays with a person.

## lowob takeaways

- **The plan is a set of rules.** Mix, upside, measures, quota, curve and crediting all need writing down.
- **Design shapes effort.** Caps, bonus timing and tiers change what each group of sellers does.
- **Quota realism comes first.** A plan built on unreachable quotas stops motivating.
- **Record rulings.** Splits and windfall decisions set precedent for the next dispute.

## Common questions

### What is a typical sales compensation pay mix?

It depends on the role. WorldatWork's 2022 survey found 54/46 for field new-account sellers, 59/41 for sellers managing current customers and 66/34 for first-line managers.

### What does 70/30/3x mean in sales compensation?

A 70% base and 30% target incentive, with up to three times the target incentive available to top performers.

### Should sales commissions be capped?

Half of organisations cap, but Steenburgh and Ahearne's research found caps lead top sellers to stop selling once they hit target. Many firms use windfall rules for unusual deals instead.

### How many measures should a sales compensation plan have?

Two or three is the norm: 71% of organisations in WorldatWork's 2022 survey used that many. More dilutes attention.

## Sources and notes

- [WorldatWork and SalesGlobe, 2022 Sales Compensation Programs and Practices](https://worldatwork.org/media/CDN/dist/CDN2/documents/pdf/resources/research/WorldatWork_RSCH_Sales-Comp-Programs-and-Practices_2022.pdf), August 2022. Professional association survey of 693 practitioners; sample sizes vary by question.
- [Alexander Group, What is a Variable Compensation Plan?](https://alexandergroup.com/?p=3350), undated. Consultancy guidance; the worked example is illustrative.
- [WorldatWork, 2023 Sales Compensation Investment Grows During Turbulent Times](https://worldatwork.org/resources/publications/workspan-daily/2023-sales-compensation-investment-grows-during-turbulent-times), 21 September 2023. Reports an Alexander Group survey of 350+ executives; self-reported projections.
- [Darden School of Business, One Size Does Not Fit All When Motivating a Sales Force](https://news.darden.virginia.edu/2012/07/18/1-size-does-not-fit-all-when-motivating-sales-force/), July 2012. University summary of Steenburgh and Ahearne's Harvard Business Review research; one company's field data.

## Related research

- [Sales Capacity and Quota Setting](https://lowob.com/research/sales-capacity-and-quota-setting/)
- [Discount Governance](https://lowob.com/research/discount-governance/)
- [Renewals and Expansion](https://lowob.com/research/renewals-and-expansion/)
- [The Ten Commercial Decisions Worth Recording](https://lowob.com/research/the-commercial-decisions-worth-recording/)
- [What Thought Leadership Actually Is](https://lowob.com/research/what-thought-leadership-actually-is/)

## Next move

Give your plan document to one seller and ask them to calculate last quarter's payout without help. Every question they need to ask is a rule the plan has not written down.

# What Is Entity Resolution?

Source: https://lowob.com/research/what-is-entity-resolution/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-28 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Revenue

> Summary: Entity resolution is the work of deciding which records describe the same real-world company or person. The statistical method most tools still rest on dates from 1969. For a commercial team it is what keeps an account's history in one place, and what stops two agents treating one buyer as two.

Entity resolution is the process of deciding which records, within one system or across several, refer to the same real-world entity, such as a company or a person. It covers deduplication inside a CRM and record linkage between systems such as the CRM, billing and support. Good entity resolution sorts each pair of records into match, non-match or "needs a person to look", and keeps the history of every merge.

*Figure: Where this piece sits in The Build Order: the context layer.*

## What entity resolution means

A firm rarely has one record per customer. The same company appears under its trading name in the CRM, its registered name with "Limited" in billing and only as a web domain in the support desk. The same buyer appears twice after changing email address. Entity resolution decides which of these belong together.

Two jobs sit under the term. **Deduplication** finds repeats inside one system. **Record linkage** connects records across systems that share no common identifier. Both rest on the same question: given two records, how likely is it that they describe the same thing?

| Entity resolution is | Entity resolution is not |
| --- | --- |
| Deciding which records describe one real entity | Enrichment, which adds new attributes from outside |
| A scored judgment with an uncertain middle band | A single exact-match rule on email address |
| Recorded, so merges can be traced and reversed | Deleting the losing record |
| Ongoing, because new duplicates arrive daily | A one-off clean-up project |

## How it works

### The 1969 model still underneath

Ivan Fellegi and Alan Sunter set out the theory in the *Journal of the American Statistical Association* in December 1969. Each pair of records is compared field by field. The pattern of agreements is scored by how likely it is among true matches versus non-matches. Two thresholds then sort pairs into three outcomes: link, non-link, or possible link where the evidence is insufficient and a person reviews it. The rule is designed to minimise how many pairs land in that middle band for a chosen error rate.

### Deterministic and probabilistic matching

Deterministic matching applies fixed rules: same email domain and same postcode means same company. It is easy to explain but misses variants. Probabilistic matching weighs partial agreement across many fields, so a near-identical name plus the same phone number can outweigh a different address.

The UK Ministry of Justice built Splink, an open-source library, to link justice data that lacks a consistent person identifier. Government guidance describes it as implementing the Fellegi-Sunter model and returning a match score between 0 and 1. The team designed it to handle around 100 million records and reported using it on problems of about 15 million records with runtimes under an hour.

### What a CRM gives you

Most CRMs ship a simpler version. Salesforce's matching rules combine exact and fuzzy methods, such as Jaro-Winkler distance for first names and edit distance for street names. Duplicate rules then decide whether to block the save or warn and allow it. Each object can have up to five active matching rules. This handles entry-time duplicates well and cross-system linkage poorly.

## Why it matters for a commercial team

Account history is only useful if it is in one place. A win-loss review that misses half a client's deals because they sit under a second account record draws the wrong conclusion. In **lowob**'s model, the CRM is the store and the decision record sits on top of it; both depend on knowing which account a decision belongs to.

Agents make the cost visible. A sales agent working from two records for one buyer can enrol the same person in two sequences, or quote two prices. An agent at autonomy level 2 or above should not run against accounts whose identity is unresolved.

> An unresolved duplicate in a report is an error. An unresolved duplicate read by an agent is two actions.

## How to start

| Step | What to do | Who owns it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pick the entity | Start with accounts, not contacts; fewer records, higher value | Revenue operations |
| Choose match fields | Domain, registered name, company number, billing address | Revenue operations |
| Set two thresholds | Auto-merge above the upper one, review between, ignore below | Revenue operations with sales lead |
| Staff the middle band | A named person reviews possible matches weekly | Revenue operations |
| Merge without deleting | Keep the losing record as superseded, with a pointer to the survivor | System rule |
| Measure | Count new duplicates created each month | Revenue operations |

Two mistakes recur. One is setting the auto-merge threshold low to clear the queue, which merges subsidiaries into parents and loses their separate contracts. The other is deleting the merged record, which breaks links from old emails, invoices and decisions. Mark it superseded instead.

## lowob takeaways

- **Identity before automation.** Agents should not act on accounts whose records are unresolved.
- **Respect the middle band.** Possible matches go to a person, as Fellegi and Sunter proposed in 1969.
- **Merge, never delete.** Keep the superseded record so history and decisions stay attached.
- **Start with accounts.** Company records are fewer and carry more value than contacts.

## Common questions

### What is the difference between entity resolution and deduplication?

Deduplication finds repeated records inside one system. Entity resolution is the wider task, including linking records about the same entity across different systems.

### What is probabilistic record linkage?

A method that scores how likely two records are to match by weighing agreement across several fields, rather than requiring exact matches on one field.

### Can a CRM do entity resolution on its own?

For entry-time duplicates, mostly yes, through matching and duplicate rules. Linking the CRM with billing, support and product data usually needs a separate tool or warehouse process.

### Why does entity resolution matter for AI agents?

Agents act on records directly. Two records for one buyer can produce two outreach sequences, conflicting quotes or a history that looks thinner than it is.

## Sources and notes

- [Fellegi and Sunter, A Theory for Record Linkage](https://cs.cornell.edu/~shmat/courses/cs6434/fellegi-sunter.pdf), Journal of the American Statistical Association, Vol. 64, No. 328, December 1969. Foundational academic paper; course-hosted copy.
- [UK Government, Splink: MoJ's open source library for probabilistic record linkage at scale](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/joined-up-data-in-government-the-future-of-data-linking-methods/splink-mojs-open-source-library-for-probabilistic-record-linkage-at-scale), first published August 2020, updated July 2021. Scale figures are the team's own and dated.
- [Salesforce Trailhead, Duplicate Management: matching and duplicate rules](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/sales_admin_duplicate_management/sales_admin_duplicate_management_unit_2). Vendor documentation; other CRMs offer comparable features.

## Related research

- [What Is CRM Data Hygiene?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-crm-data-hygiene/)
- [Your CRM Is Memory, Not a Brain](https://lowob.com/research/your-crm-is-memory-not-a-brain/)
- [Supersede, Never Overwrite](https://lowob.com/research/supersede-never-overwrite/)
- [What Is a System of Record?](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-system-of-record/)

## Next move

Export your account list and sort it by website domain. Count the domains that appear on more than one account; that number is your starting duplicate rate.

# Prompt Engineering vs Context Engineering

Source: https://lowob.com/research/prompt-engineering-vs-context-engineering/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-27 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Strategy

> Summary: Prompt engineering is the craft of writing and structuring instructions for a model. Context engineering is the wider job of deciding what the model sees at every step: instructions, retrieved records, tool results and history. Prompting fixes format and tone; context fixes accuracy. For agents and commercial work, context is usually the bigger lever.

Prompt engineering is the practice of writing and structuring a model's instructions so its output meets a requirement. Context engineering is the wider practice of choosing everything the model sees at each step: instructions, retrieved documents and records, tool results and conversation history. Prompting mostly fixes format, tone and task framing. Context mostly fixes accuracy. A well-written prompt cannot rescue a model that was handed the wrong facts.

*Figure: Where this piece sits in The Build Order: the context layer.*

## What the two terms mean

[Prompt engineering](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-prompt-engineering/) is about the instructions. OpenAI's guide lists its main techniques: separating developer instructions from user input, marking sections with Markdown or XML tags, giving a few input and output examples, and pinning production apps to a dated model snapshot so behaviour does not shift underneath them. Anthropic's guide lists clarity, examples, XML structure, role prompting and prompt chaining. The work product is a template.

[Context engineering](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-context-engineering/) is about the whole state the model works from. Anthropic's September 2025 engineering post defines it as "the set of strategies for curating and maintaining the optimal set of tokens (information) during LLM inference." The guiding principle is to find the "smallest possible set of high-signal tokens" that makes the desired outcome likely. For an agent that runs many steps, that state changes at every step, so the work is continuous.

The two are nested rather than opposed. Anthropic describes prompt engineering as "methods for writing and organizing LLM instructions" and treats it as one part of the larger job. Even OpenAI's prompt guide crosses the line: it recommends adding proprietary data to the prompt through retrieval, which is a context decision.

|  | Prompt engineering | Context engineering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Question it answers | How should the instruction be written? | What should the model see at this step? |
| Main inputs | Instructions, examples, output format | Instructions plus retrieved records, tool results, history, memory |
| Done | Once per template, then revised | At every step of a task |
| Who does it | Whoever owns the use case | Use-case owner with data and systems owners |
| Fixes | Format, tone, structure, task framing | Accuracy, relevance, currency of facts |
| Typical failure | Ambiguous instruction, inconsistent format | Missing, stale or irrelevant data in the window |
| Typical tools | Templates, few-shot examples, a [system prompt](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-system-prompt/) | Retrieval, connectors, compaction, notes, sub-agents |
| Scales with | Model capability | Data quality and permissions |

## Why context became the bigger lever

The shift came with agents. An agent calls tools and accumulates history across many steps, so the material entering its window grows with every step, and most of it was never written by the person who wrote the prompt.

More material does not help on its own. Chroma's research team tested 18 models in 2025 and found that "model performance consistently degrades with increasing input length," even on simple tasks. "Even a single distractor reduces performance relative to the baseline." Anthropic calls this context rot and describes a model's attention as a finite budget. A larger [context window](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-context-window/) raises the ceiling but does not remove the need to choose.

That is why Anthropic's techniques for long-running agents are context techniques, not wording techniques:

- **Just-in-time retrieval:** keep lightweight references, such as record IDs, and load the data only when it is needed.
- **Compaction:** summarise a long session and continue in a fresh window with the summary.
- **Structured notes:** write notes outside the window and read them back later.
- **Sub-agents:** delegate focused work to agents with clean context that return condensed results.

None of these change how the instruction is phrased. All of them change what the model reads.

## Which one your problem needs

Diagnose the failure before choosing the fix. Anthropic's prompting guide makes the same point: start with "a clear definition of the success criteria" and "some ways to empirically test against those criteria."

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Right facts, wrong format or tone | Instruction | Prompt: examples and an explicit output format |
| Ignores part of the instruction | Instruction buried or ambiguous | Prompt: separate sections, put the rule first |
| States an outdated price or owner | Stale data in context | Context: retrieve from the system of record |
| Contradicts what was agreed last month | Decision missing from context | Context: include decision records for the account |
| Good on short tasks, worse on long ones | Context rot | Context: compaction, notes, sub-agents |
| Different answers for different users on the same question | Different data or definitions reached the model | Context: shared definitions and [permission-aware retrieval](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-permission-aware-retrieval/) |
| Too slow or too costly | Model or volume | Neither first; try a different model, as Anthropic suggests |

Three mistakes recur on commercial teams:

- **Prompt libraries as strategy.** A shared folder of clever prompts helps with format. It does nothing about a CRM full of stale fields.
- **Connecting everything.** Giving an assistant every system and letting it sort them out fills the window with distractors.
- **No test set.** Without twenty real questions and agreed good answers, neither prompt nor context changes can be judged.

## The **lowob** view

In **lowob**'s enterprise brain loop of store, wiring, record, reasoning and learning, prompt engineering belongs to reasoning. It shapes how the model works on what it is given. Context engineering is the wiring: it decides which slice of the store and the record reaches the model for each task. Rent the tooling for both, but own the choices about what each task should see.

The highest-value context on the commercial line is usually the decision record: what was agreed, by whom, why and with what expected outcome. A model that sees it will not reopen settled questions or quote a superseded discount. A model that does not see it will, however good the prompt.

## lowob takeaways

- **Prompts shape the output; context decides its accuracy.** Fix wording problems with prompts and fact problems with context.
- **Context is nested around the prompt.** The instruction is one input among the records, tool results and history the model reads.
- **Less, chosen well, beats more.** Accuracy falls as irrelevant material grows, even in large windows.
- **Test before tuning either.** Written success criteria and a small question set come first.

## Common questions

### What is the difference between prompt engineering and context engineering?

Prompt engineering is writing and structuring a model's instructions. Context engineering covers everything the model sees at each step, including retrieved records, tool results and history, and manages it as the task runs.

### Is context engineering replacing prompt engineering?

No. Anthropic describes it as a natural progression that includes prompt engineering. Good instructions still matter; they are one part of the context.

### When is prompt engineering enough?

When the model already has the right facts and the problem is format, tone or task framing. Short, single-step tasks with stable inputs often need nothing more.

### How do I know whether my AI problem is a prompt or a context problem?

Check the failures against a test set. Wrong format or tone points to the prompt. Wrong, outdated or contradictory facts point to the context.

- [Anthropic, Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents), 29 September 2025. Vendor engineering guidance.
- [Chroma, Context rot: how increasing input tokens impacts LLM performance](https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot), 14 July 2025. Vendor research; Chroma sells retrieval infrastructure.
